Notes: 1897 census: about 1,508 Jews, 59% of total population
1921: 463 Jews, 50% of total population (after town passed to Poland)
Estimated about 2000 Jews on eve of war including refugees from occupied Poland; German occupation 28 June 1941; about 1400 killed 5-6 Aug 1941
Memorial book: Jewish population nearly 2000 before Nazi occupation; mostly artisans and tradesmen; 5 survivors named; no ghetto per this account

Ghetto July-August 1941 headed by Avraham Levin and Moshe Kaplan; 6-7 Aug 1941 about 1400 Jews shot near Grechishche plus about 500 more on Yanki Kupaly Street (execution tolls); Jews were almost half of prewar population incl. Polish refugees

Yizkor book intro: community said to be founded toward end of 15th century (tradition; not dated by documents); almost entire Jewish population of 2000 annihilated August 1941; town burned by Russian soldiers 1915
Organized Jewish community: Jews fled to forest as town burned in WWI around Yom Kippur; glassworks built 1895; community rebuilt in interwar Poland with American Jewish aid
Soviet period 1939-1941: Rabbi Glick received authority from departing Polish police; Jewish youth in Chalutz Left Poalei Zion and Communist groups; organized community
